newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo port opens new oil jetty ahead of P&O deal.
newsitem.headline: Colombo port opens new oil jetty ahead of P&O deal.

text.p: The Colombo port, south Asia's trans-shipment hub, will open a new oil jetty on its island breakwater on Friday, a spokesman for the Sri Lanka Ports Authority (SLPA) said on Friday.
The oil jetty was shifted from its original position at the port's north pier to allow the latter to be developed into a terminal for unloading conventional cargo, he said.

SLPA officials said the use of the north pier for conventional cargo will free the port's Queen Elizabeth Quay which is to be leased to a consortium led by Britain's Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co.

The SLPA is currently holding talks with P&O on plans to expand capacity by developing the Queen Elizabeth Quay into a container terminal and later build a new port adjacent to the existing one at a cost of up to $1 billion.
Colombo port, which has a capacity of 1.6 million containers, last year handled almost 1.4 million containers, up 29 percent from 1995.
Trans-shipment traffic accounts for about 70 percent of the port's throughput.
